_comment: EUR per kWh. 'solar' is NOT zero: self-consumed PV forgoes the feed-in tariff, so its marginal cost is the feed-in rate (or LCOE if you prefer the full-cost view).

solar-de-feed-in.label: Germany PV self-consumption, opportunity cost = feed-in tariff <=10 kWp (Aug 2026-Jan 2027)

solar-de-lcoe.label: Germany small rooftop PV (<=30 kWp) LCOE, mid-range of 6.3-14.4 ct/kWh (Fraunhofer ISE, Jul 2024)

_co2_comment: gCO2/kWh per tariff. Grid figures use the DIRECT-COMBUSTION convention (what the official national inventories publish); the PV figures are LIFECYCLE (there is no combustion to measure). Mixing the two conventions understates the grid slightly -- the lifecycle-consistent German figure is 406 gCO2eq/kWh, not 344. See docs/CO2_ESTIMATE.md.

co2_g_per_kwh_sources.grid-de-household: 344 g/kWh, German grid mix 2025 (estimate vintage), Umweltbundesamt CC 16/2026, published Mar 2026: https://www.umweltbundesamt.de/system/files/medien/11850/publikationen/2026-03/16_2026_CC.pdf -- series: 2023 final 379, 2024 preliminary 353, 2025 estimate 344. Preliminary vintages get revised by up to ~10 g. Lifecycle equivalent: 406 gCO2eq/kWh.
co2_g_per_kwh_sources.grid-us-avg: 350 g/kWh, US national average: EPA eGRID2023 rev2 (published 12 Jun 2025, data year 2023) CO2e total output rate 770.884 lb/MWh = 349.7 g/kWh -- https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2025-06/summary_tables_rev2.pdf . EIA Electricity Profile (data year 2024) gives 785 lb/MWh = 356 g/kWh. eGRID2024 not released as of Sep 2026.
co2_g_per_kwh_sources.solar-de-feed-in: 40 g/kWh lifecycle emissions for rooftop PV (Fraunhofer ISE class figure) -- see docs/sources.md.
co2_g_per_kwh_sources.solar-de-lcoe: 40 g/kWh lifecycle emissions for rooftop PV (Fraunhofer ISE class figure) -- see docs/sources.md.

cloud_inference_co2_estimate._comment: *** ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE ESTIMATE, NOT A MEASUREMENT. *** No cloud AI provider publishes energy per token, so unlike every other number in this file this one cannot be sourced to a vendor figure -- it is reconstructed from published per-query estimates divided by an assumed response length. Treat it as accurate to within roughly a factor of 3, and do not quote it as a fact about any specific provider. Full derivation, sources and error bars: docs/CO2_ESTIMATE.md.
cloud_inference_co2_estimate.wh_per_mtok_it_source: ESTIMATE, derived not measured: Epoch AI (7 Feb 2025) estimates a typical GPT-4o ChatGPT query at ~0.3 Wh and states its assumption of 500 output tokens per query -- https://epoch.ai/gradient-updates/how-much-energy-does-chatgpt-use -- which gives 0.3 Wh / 500 tok = 600 Wh per 1M OUTPUT tokens. This is a bottom-up model (200B-param MoE, H100s, 10% utilisation), not a measurement. Jegham et al., 'How Hungry is AI?' (arXiv:2505.09598) measures GPT-4o short prompts at 0.423 Wh / 300 output tok = ~1410 Wh/1M, i.e. 2.4x higher. Google's production-measured median Gemini text prompt of 0.24 Wh (arXiv:2508.15734) is the only in-production figure but publishes NO token counts, so it cannot be converted per-token. Defensible range: 600-1500 Wh per 1M output tokens; 600 is the low end of it.
cloud_inference_co2_estimate.pue_label: PUE 1.13 (hyperscale fleet average; Google 1.09, AWS 1.14, Microsoft 1.17)
cloud_inference_co2_estimate.pue_source: Midpoint of the three fleet-wide figures the largest cloud providers publish: Google 1.09 CY2025 TTM (https://datacenters.google/efficiency/), AWS 1.14 global CY2025 (https://sustainability.aboutamazon.com/products-services/aws-cloud), Microsoft 1.17 FY25 (https://datacenters.microsoft.com/sustainability/efficiency/ -- note the widely-quoted 1.18 is Microsoft's stale 2022 first disclosure). All three exclude or obscure leased colo capacity, and the reporting periods are not like-for-like. The industry-wide Uptime Institute 2026 average is far worse at 1.52, but hyperscale AI serving does not run in an average facility.
cloud_inference_co2_estimate.confidence: LOW -- the grid and PUE inputs are solid, but the energy-per-token input is a derived estimate good to roughly a factor of 2-3 upward. It is a magnitude, not a measurement.
cloud_inference_co2_estimate.basis: Epoch AI's ~0.3 Wh/query at its own stated 500 output tokens/query, x datacentre PUE, x published grid carbon intensity.
cloud_inference_co2_estimate._regions_comment: NOTE, against the common assumption: the big US AI-datacentre regions are NOT dirtier than the US average. Northern Virginia ('Data Center Alley') is ~20-30% CLEANER thanks to ~28-40% nuclear and almost no coal, and gas-heavy ERCOT still lands slightly below the national average because wind+solar supply ~28% of it. A 'US AI industry runs on gas, therefore dirty' framing is not supported by the published grid data.

us-avg.label: US national average grid mix (EPA eGRID2023)
us-avg.source: EPA eGRID2023 rev2 (published 12 Jun 2025, data year 2023): CO2e total output rate 770.884 lb/MWh = 349.7 g/kWh -- https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2025-06/summary_tables_rev2.pdf

us-virginia.label: Northern Virginia 'Data Center Alley' (eGRID SRVC) -- CLEANER than the US average
us-virginia.source: EPA eGRID2023 subregion SRVC ~270 g/kWh; EIA state profile for Virginia (data year 2024) gives 286 g/kWh -- https://www.eia.gov/electricity/state/virginia/ . Driven by ~28-40% nuclear and only ~1.9% coal. CAVEAT: Virginia imports ~30% of the electricity it consumes from the dirtier western PJM pool (eGRID RFCW, ~416 g/kWh), so a consumption-based figure would be materially higher than this generation-based one.

us-ercot.label: Texas / ERCOT (eGRID ERCT) -- gas-heavy but near the US average
us-ercot.source: EPA eGRID2023 subregion ERCT ~334 g/kWh; EIA state profile for Texas (data year 2024) gives 373 g/kWh -- https://www.eia.gov/electricity/state/texas/ . Gas supplies ~50% of generation, but wind+solar supply ~28.5%, which is why a 'gas-heavy' grid still lands at or below the national average.

de-grid.label: German grid mix (UBA 2025) -- the same-grid comparison
de-grid.source: Umweltbundesamt CC 16/2026, published Mar 2026: 344 gCO2/kWh for 2025 (estimate vintage) -- https://www.umweltbundesamt.de/system/files/medien/11850/publikationen/2026-03/16_2026_CC.pdf . Same figure as the grid-de-household tariff; use it to compare cloud vs. local hardware on the SAME grid, isolating the hardware-efficiency difference from the grid-mix difference.
